What are the processes used to identify work- related hazards and assess risks on a routine and non-routine basis by the entity?

The Company recognizes that the identification of work-related hazards and the assessment of associated risks are fundamental to maintaining a safe and healthy workplace. Work-related hazards are identified and assessed for both routine and non- routine activities through periodic Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment (HIRA) workshops conducted at the site and departmental levels. These assessments include reviews of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), supported by electrical safety audits, random load inspections, and sampling audits to evaluate the effectiveness of existing controls and identify emerging risks. For non-routine activities, the Company follows a structured Permit-to-Work system with pre-job risk assessments for activities such as hot work, confined space entry, and work at height.
